content: The recommended daily intake of fiber is 2 grams per day, as indicated for use as a daily fiber supplement. According to the Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics (2015), the daily recommended total fiber intake is as follows: 19 grams per day for children aged 1 to 3 years and 25 grams per day for children aged 4 to 8 years. Psyllium may reduce the levels or effectiveness of intranasal metoclopramide through an unspecified mechanism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. Co-administration of intranasal metoclopramide with drugs that impair gastrointestinal (GI) motility may decrease the systemic absorption of metoclopramide, potentially reducing its therapeutic effect. Close monitoring is necessary in such cases. Psyllium may also decrease the effects of sodium picosulfate through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. Potential side effects of psyllium include abdominal cramping, constipation, flatulence, and fecal impaction. Rare but serious adverse effects include hypersensitivity reactions, GI obstruction, fecal impaction, symptoms resembling appendicitis or an acute surgical abdomen, GI ulceration, dysphagia, and rectal bleeding. Patients with phenylketonuria should be aware that sugar-free psyllium products may contain phenylalanine. Psyllium is classified as Pregnancy Category B, meaning that controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. During lactation, there is no available data, but since psyllium is not absorbed systemically, it is unlikely to pose a risk to breastfeeding infants.
